## TL;DR

Task #1098 makes common agent failures visible where board users need them. Known authentication, unavailable-model, usage-limit, and network errors now have plain-language explanations and next steps. Failed task cards and drawers retain the CLI output behind a disclosure, the Agents page shows the last run and its reason, and signed-out or unavailable-model failures create a deduplicated board notice per CLI. A later successful run clears that CLI notice. Crash-recovery activity also uses the same explanation while retaining the original error. The required changed-scope check passed.

## Work and rationale

I continued from the branch's existing implementation after RepoOS reported that a prior handoff failed because `.repoos/engineering-report-drafts/1098.md` was absent. The task implementation and a review pass were already present in the branch. I read the task specification and latest review report, then checked the classifier, notification integration, crash-recovery copy, UI last-run surface, tests, and documentation in the current tree before addressing the handoff blocker.

The shared classifier in `src/core/agent-failure.ts` recognizes common signed-out and expired-token messages, model-unavailable errors (including Cursor's `Cannot use this model` text), usage limits, network failures, and Copilot Auto-tier errors. It returns a stable reason id, concise summary, and suggested fix. Known reasons retain the raw CLI tail in a delimited form so the card and drawer can separate user guidance from diagnostic detail; unknown failures continue to fall back to their raw detail. Existing Copilot-specific enrichment remains in place and feeds the shared classification path.

The server invokes notification handling for failed runs and clears a CLI's current notice after a clean run. Notice identity is keyed by CLI, so another failed task updates the existing board item rather than adding one notice per task. The notification logic limits these notices to authentication and unavailable-model failures; usage-limit failures and transient network errors already have their own handling or are not durable setup problems. The task card and drawer display the concise reason with the CLI output available on demand. The Agents endpoint and page expose last-run status and the formatted failure reason. Crash recovery formats the raw reason before writing its switch/resume activity, so the reason remains understandable after the selected agent changes.

I made two small follow-ups from the review notes. I corrected the failure-message documentation heading and expanded the note to describe the card disclosure, board bell notice, and Agents last-run display. I also preserved a provider-supplied `until HH:MM` value in the user-facing usage-limit summary, with a regression assertion. This keeps a useful reset time without adding provider-specific parsing or changing the underlying raw error.

The classifier tests exercise signed-out wording across supported CLIs, Cursor model rejection, Copilot Auto-tier unavailability, usage-limit timing, network errors, unknown-error fallback, and preservation of raw CLI detail. Existing attention-notification tests exercise deduplication, successful-run clearing, and suppression of network and usage-limit cases from the durable per-agent notice. These tests use local stores and fixtures; no live network call is needed.

## Approaches tried

I followed the existing Copilot enrichment pattern and kept classification as a small shared core helper rather than duplicating regular expressions in each agent role. That provides the same result for engineer, reviewer, PM, debugger, and other run paths as long as they use the shared failure formatting. I reused the existing attention event store and bell flow instead of introducing a separate notification channel or a new persistence mechanism. The notice uses a stable per-CLI id; its detail is replaced on repeated failures, and clean completion removes that id.

For presentation, I kept the CLI error available in the task experience but placed it behind the existing disclosure affordance. This lets the normal view emphasize cause and action while keeping enough detail to diagnose cases the classifier does not fully explain. Unknown output remains usable as a raw fallback rather than being hidden or converted to a misleading generic cause.

## Challenges and blockers

The original task handoff was rejected before review finalization because its engineer-authored report draft was missing. I created this draft after completing verification, as requested, so RepoOS can finalize it and bind it to the checked tree.

The first remote validation host (`thinkpad`) hung during its container run. RepoOS removed that validation container and retried on `bee`; the retry completed successfully. The local check then completed its remaining guards and user-docs build. There were no code or test failures to resolve. The build emitted its existing large-chunk advisory and the docs build noted a missing unrelated sidebar anchor; both builds completed successfully.

## Key learnings

Failure language needs to remain useful at more than one level: the task surface should quickly say what happened and what action is available, while support/debugging still needs the provider's unmodified tail. A shared classifier makes those summaries consistent across run roles and lets crash recovery reuse the same wording. Notice identity should follow the agent/CLI rather than the task because authentication and account model availability affect every task using that CLI. Clearing that notice on the next successful run provides a direct recovery signal without asking users to dismiss stale warnings manually.

Verification ran with `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. RepoOS reported the remote build and scoped tests passed on its retry host, the local build/staleness and formatting/lint guards passed, the rendered contrast audit and UI smoke test passed, and the changed user documentation built successfully. No live provider or network integration was exercised.
